subject: Evaluation kickoff and Redwood runbook for Sentinel Analytics model-fit
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@sentinel.ai>, Marcus Reed <marcus@sentinel.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & next steps: small-scale eval on Redwood (dataset + scoring)

Hi Samira / Marcus —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a representative eval run on Redwood next week. Goal is to validate model fit for your "case intake summarization" flow and measure regression risk vs your current heuristic pipeline.

High-level ask from your side: a ~500–1,000 example seeddataset (CSV) with the following columns: id, raw_text, expected_summary, case_type, pii_flag (Y/N), source_timestamp. If there are protected records, mark pii_flag=Y and we will run those on a private tenant if you prefer (see options below).

What we'll run on Redwood (recommended starting set):
- redwood/realtime-3b (baseline low-latency)
- redwood/rl-7b-instruct (recommended for higher-fidelity summaries with temperature=0.2)
- redwood/opt-1.3b-q4 as a cost-efficient comparison

Evaluation metrics & pass criteria (proposed):
- Structured summary exact-match on extracted fields (case_type): goal >= 88% exact-match
- Token-level F1 for key-phrase extraction (entities): target >= 0.80
- Semantic similarity for open summaries: average cosine(embedding) >= 0.86 vs expected_summary (we use Redwood embeddings for consistency)
- Latency: p95 generation time <= 450ms for realtime-3b on the dev preset

Attachments included: sentinel_eval_template.csv (dataset template), sentinel_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (initial prompts and temperature/stop settings), sentinel_scoring_guide.md (scoring scripts & example outputs).

Security & data-handling choices: if your dataset includes PHI we can run the eval on Redwood Private (VPC) or a Dedicated cluster — let us know which. By default we will run on Hosted with ephemeral caching disabled for the seed run.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) You share the seed CSV by Friday 10/23.
2) We run a small smoke eval (200 rows) and share a result dashboard + raw scorer output by EOD 10/26.
3) Review results together and decide whether to expand to 1k examples or to try a quantized variant.

If this looks good I'll CC Laura from Customer Success to schedule the kickoff slot and hand off the scoring runner.

Cheers,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: small-scale eval on Redwood (dataset + scoring)

Thanks Jordan — this is very helpful. Two quick questions before we send the export: 

1) PII/PHI: Our current intake snapshots sometimes include SSNs and patient names. If we mark pii_flag=Y can you confirm which environment you’ll run those rows in and how long Redwood retains any model outputs for the eval?

2) Scoring: For the semantic similarity threshold you mentioned (0.86), what embedding model + dimensionality do you use? We want to ensure comparability with our internal checks.

Also timeline: Friday export is OK but we may only be able to deliver 400 rows initially; does that materially change the smoke-run plan?

— Samira
Product Lead, Sentinel Analytics

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@sentinel.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T13:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: small-scale eval on Redwood (dataset + scoring)

Samira —

Great questions. Short answers below, and I attached a short scoring-run README in sentinel_scoring_guide.md with exact commands we’ll use.

1) PII/PHI handling: If you mark pii_flag=Y we will not run those rows on Hosted unless you explicitly approve; the default for pii_flag=Y is Redwood Private (VPC) or a Dedicated cluster. For Hosted runs we default to ephemeral log retention (14 days) and you can request log suppression. For Private/Dedicated we can set log retention to 0 and integrate with your KMS.

2) Embedding model: we compute semantic similarity with redwood/emb-sim-1 (1536-d) and cosine similarity. The 0.86 threshold is conservative; we can expose the raw scores so you can tune. The scoring guide includes a sample scoring.py that computes token-F1, exact-match and embedding cosine.

3) Dataset size: 400 rows is fine. We'll run the 200-row smoke first (random sample) and then the full 400. The dashboard reports are robust to sample size; smaller N just increases CI.

Logistics / kickoff: Laura will schedule a 30-minute slot tomorrow to walk through the scoring guide and access details (S3/Drive upload, or secure ShareFile if you prefer).

Ben + I will queue three model variants and a quantized run. Ben — can you confirm the dev cluster preset (p95 latency target) and whether to enable KV prefix caching for this workload?

Thanks,
Jordan

[Attachment: sentinel_scoring_guide.md (MD, 4 KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: small-scale eval on Redwood (dataset + scoring)

Jordan — quick internal note back to the thread so Samira sees the config we plan to use.

Planned run configuration (dev preset):
- Cluster: Dedicated-dev-1 (gpu: a2-highmem-1 equivalent)
- KV prefix caching: ON for warm-start examples (improves token cost by ~12% for repeated prefixes)
- Batching: continuous batching disabled for smoke (to measure single-request latency), enabled for the 400-row run (batch size target 8)
- Quantization: run the q4_0 pass on opt-1.3b-q4 to measure cost vs quality delta
- Logging: Hosted run for non-pii rows with 14-day ephemeral logs; pii_flag=Y rows run on Dedicated-dev-1 with retention=0, KMS encrypt at-rest

Model variants queued: redwood/realtime-3b, redwood/rl-7b-instruct, redwood/opt-1.3b-q4 (q4_0).

I'll kick the smoke job once we have the 200-row slice and the signed NDA (if any). Laura will send the calendar invite for the scoping call.

— Ben
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
